equipo-patrocinador-principal.queEs: A company partners with one specific team for the whole season and appears in everything that team does.
equipo-patrocinador-principal.queRecibe: Its brand on the match shirt, a mention in every squad list and line-up, and a place in the team photos.

equipo-empresa-del-mes.queEs: Each month a different company takes centre stage at the club: it is introduced, with what it does and why it backs the team.
equipo-empresa-del-mes.queRecibe: A full month of visibility: an introduction post, mentions at that month's matches and its logo in the monthly round-up.

equipo-patrocinador-de-partido.queEs: A single match carries a company's name. It works for the derby, the club day or any big fixture.
equipo-patrocinador-de-partido.queRecibe: Its brand on the match poster, on the PA during the game and in the result post.

equipo-desplazamientos.queEs: A company covers the team's trips to away matches, with money or by providing the transport.
equipo-desplazamientos.queRecibe: Its brand linked to every trip, with departure and arrival posts, and on the coach if it provides it.

equipo-material.queEs: Balls, cones, bibs, first-aid kit: a team's working equipment for a season.
equipo-material.queRecibe: Its brand on the equipment and in training posts, which are the club's most frequent.

equipo-empresa-oficial.titulo: The club's official company in its sector
equipo-empresa-oficial.queEs: One company is the only one in its sector linked to the club: the official accountant, the official clinic, the official bakery.
equipo-empresa-oficial.queRecibe: Exclusivity in its sector for the season and the right to call itself the club's official company in its own advertising.

equipo-contenido-con-jugadores.queEs: The players appear in a piece of content featuring the company's product or service.
equipo-contenido-con-jugadores.queRecibe: A piece filmed at the club, with club people, that the company can also use on its own social media.

equipo-entrenamiento-abierto.queEs: A training session open to the public, hosted by the company: families, members and the company's customers are invited.
equipo-entrenamiento-abierto.queRecibe: An afternoon with its brand in front of the club's families, with the chance to bring samples or set up its own stand.

equipacion-pecho.queEs: The most visible spot of all, the one in every photo and every broadcast.
equipacion-pecho.queRecibe: Its logo on the front of the match shirt for the whole season.

equipacion-espalda.queEs: The second most expensive spot, and the easiest to read from the stands.
equipacion-espalda.queRecibe: Its logo on the back of the match shirt for the whole season.

equipacion-manga.queEs: A small, more affordable spot, perfect for a local shop that can't go for the front.
equipacion-manga.queRecibe: Its logo on the sleeve of the match shirt for the whole season.

equipacion-pantalon.queEs: Another spot almost no club sells, usually because it never occurs to them that it can be sold.
equipacion-pantalon.queRecibe: Its logo on the match shorts for the whole season.

equipacion-entrenamiento.queEs: It's seen less at matches, but it's worn four days a week instead of one.
equipacion-entrenamiento.queRecibe: Its logo on the training kit, the one that shows up most in everyday posts.

equipacion-chandal.queEs: What the players wear to arrive at the ground, to travel and to walk around town.
equipacion-chandal.queRecibe: Its logo on the clothes that leave the sports ground and are seen on the street.

equipacion-mochilas.queEs: Every player takes theirs to school, college and work for years.
equipacion-mochilas.queRecibe: Its brand on an object used every day and outside the sports setting.

equipacion-presentacion.queEs: The day the new shirt is unveiled is the content with the widest reach of the whole season. It can be sold as a whole.
equipacion-presentacion.queRecibe: Being the brand that presents the kit: photo shoot, video and launch post.

instalaciones-lona.queEs: Fixed advertising on the pitch, court or sports hall, visible at every home match.
instalaciones-lona.queRecibe: Its brand in front of everyone who passes through the ground during the season, at training sessions too.

instalaciones-naming.titulo: Naming rights to the hall or ground
instalaciones-naming.queEs: The venue takes the company's name in everything the club publishes.
instalaciones-naming.queRecibe: Its name in every squad list, every match report and every mention of where the game is played.

instalaciones-vinilo-pista.queEs: A decal on the playing surface itself, which shows up in every action photo.
instalaciones-vinilo-pista.queRecibe: Presence inside the playing area, which is where the cameras and phones point.

instalaciones-marcador.queEs: The company appears on the scoreboard: the spot everyone looks at several times a match.
instalaciones-marcador.queRecibe: Its brand on the most-watched element of the venue, at every home match.

instalaciones-vestuario.queEs: The dressing room is branded with the company. A space nobody sells and the players see every day.
instalaciones-vestuario.queRecibe: Presence where the team spends most of its time, and in the before- and after-match photos.

instalaciones-entrada.queEs: The first thing anyone coming to watch a match sees.
instalaciones-entrada.queRecibe: Its brand at the entrance, in front of every spectator, home and away.

instalaciones-stand.titulo: Company stand on a match day
instalaciones-stand.queEs: The company sets up a table or a small stand at a home match.
instalaciones-stand.queRecibe: Talking face to face with the club's families, handing out samples or signing up customers on the spot.

instalaciones-megafonia.queEs: The announcer names the company at set moments of the match: line-ups, half-time, full time.
instalaciones-megafonia.queRecibe: Several spoken mentions per match, in front of the whole crowd.

intervalo-patrocinador-del-descanso.queEs: The whole half-time break carries a company's name for the full season, at one team's home matches. The club chooses which: the men's and women's first teams are sold separately, to two different companies if it likes.
intervalo-patrocinador-del-descanso.queRecibe: The announcer opening and closing every half-time with its name, its brand on whatever is set up during those minutes and a mention in the match post.

intervalo-sorteo.queEs: At half-time something is raffled among the crowd. The company provides the prize: a voucher, a dinner, one of its products.
intervalo-sorteo.queRecibe: Its product in a neighbour's hands in front of the whole stand, and its name repeated on the PA before, during and after the draw.

intervalo-reto-de-tiro.queEs: A spectator comes onto the court at half-time and tries a shot. If it goes in, the company gives them the prize; if not, they still get a small gift.
intervalo-reto-de-tiro.queRecibe: The most talked-about moment of the match with its name on it, and a short video the company can post on its own social media.

intervalo-minipartido-cantera.queEs: The club's youngest teams play for a few minutes on the main court during half-time, with their families in the stands.
intervalo-minipartido-cantera.queRecibe: Its brand on the mini-match and the photos of the kids playing on the first team's court, which are the most shared of the whole club.

intervalo-degustacion.queEs: A bakery, an ice-cream shop, a bar or any food business hands out samples to the crowd during half-time.
intervalo-degustacion.queRecibe: The whole neighbourhood trying its product on the same day, without putting on a fair or renting a stall.

intervalo-entrega-mvp.queEs: Someone from the company comes down to the court and presents the award to the best player of the match in front of the crowd.
intervalo-entrega-mvp.queRecibe: Appearing in person in the award photo, which the club, the player and often the local paper all publish.

intervalo-photocall.queEs: A backdrop with the club crest and the company's brand, set up courtside so people can take photos at half-time.
intervalo-photocall.queRecibe: Its logo in every photo the crowd posts that afternoon, shared by the fans themselves rather than the club.

intervalo-anuncio-en-pista.queEs: During the half-time minutes the company's advert plays on the PA, or its video is shown if the hall has a screen.
intervalo-anuncio-en-pista.queRecibe: A full advert, not a passing mention, with the stands full and no match to watch.

redes-publicaciones-semanales.queEs: A fixed number of posts a month in which the company appears.
redes-publicaciones-semanales.queRecibe: Repeated visibility in front of the club's community, who are local people, not bought followers.

redes-stories-partido.queEs: The company rides along with the live match coverage: preview, half-time, result.
redes-stories-partido.queRecibe: Showing up at the moment of the week with most attention, when people are waiting for the result.

redes-reel-patrocinado.queEs: A short video made by the club with the company at its centre.
redes-reel-patrocinado.queRecibe: A piece designed around its brand, with club people, which it can also post itself.

redes-sorteo.queEs: The club gives away one of the company's products or services among its followers.
redes-sorteo.queRecibe: New followers and people who get to know its business, in exchange for a product rather than money.

redes-codigo-descuento.titulo: Discount code for the club community
redes-codigo-descuento.queEs: The company offers a discount to members, families and followers, and the club spreads the word.
redes-codigo-descuento.queRecibe: New customers who arrive already identified, and a way to measure whether the sponsorship works.

redes-empresa-de-la-semana.queEs: Each week a local business that supports the club is introduced.
redes-empresa-de-la-semana.queRecibe: A dedicated post saying who they are and what they do, not just a stray logo.

redes-entrevista.titulo: Interview with the owner or the company team
redes-entrevista.queEs: The club interviews the people behind the business and publishes it as one more piece.
redes-entrevista.queRecibe: Telling its story to a local community, which is what really brings people through the door.

redes-encuesta.queEs: Score predictions, player of the match, questions to the fans: with a brand behind them.
redes-encuesta.queRecibe: Appearing in the content with the most engagement, the kind that asks for opinions.

cantera-patrocinador.queEs: A company backs the club's whole youth section: all the development teams at once.
cantera-patrocinador.queRecibe: Its brand on the youth kits and in everything posted about the development teams, which is a lot.

cantera-una-categoria.queEs: Under-10s, under-12s, under-14s: a company takes on one youth team.
cantera-una-categoria.queRecibe: An affordable option for a small shop, with that team's families as a direct audience.

cantera-empresa-amiga.queEs: A scheme for businesses that can't put in much money but want to be seen: several companies, each with a small contribution.
cantera-empresa-amiga.queRecibe: A place on the friends-of-the-club board, on the website and at the sports hall, alongside other local businesses.

cantera-material.titulo: Sports equipment for the youth teams
cantera-material.queEs: Balls, bibs and cones for the development teams, where spending is highest and budgets are lowest.
cantera-material.queRecibe: Its brand on the equipment the kids train with every week.

cantera-jugador-del-mes.queEs: A monthly award for a young player from the academy, presented by the company.
cantera-jugador-del-mes.queRecibe: Appearing in the content families share most, the kind that features their child.

cantera-jornada-especial.queEs: A day when all the youth teams play, with activities around them.
cantera-jornada-especial.queRecibe: A whole day with all the club's families in one place and its brand as host.

cantera-charla-familias.queEs: A professional gives parents a useful talk: nutrition, injuries, rest, phone use.
cantera-charla-familias.queRecibe: Presenting itself as an expert in its field in front of the families, which beats any advert.

cantera-escuela.titulo: Sponsor of the school or camp
cantera-escuela.queEs: The summer school, the Christmas camp or recruitment activities at schools.
cantera-escuela.queRecibe: Its brand on an activity that reaches children who aren't at the club yet, and their families.

jugadores-del-mes.queEs: Each month the team's best player is chosen, and a company provides and presents the award.
jugadores-del-mes.queRecibe: Its brand linked to the award, with a presentation photo and a dedicated post every month.

jugadores-patrocinado.queEs: A company sponsors one specific player for the season.
jugadores-patrocinado.queRecibe: Appearing in everything posted about that person, who at a community club is well known locally.

jugadores-visita-a-empresa.queEs: The players visit the company's premises: photos with the staff, greeting the workers, content.
jugadores-visita-a-empresa.queRecibe: A different morning for its people and its own material for social media, with the real team.

jugadores-visita-al-club.queEs: The company's staff come to a match or a training session as the club's guests.
jugadores-visita-al-club.queRecibe: An activity for its staff that takes no effort to organise, with dressing-room access and a photo with the team.

jugadores-prueba-de-producto.queEs: The team tries something from the company and says how it went: drinks, footwear, recovery, nutrition.
jugadores-prueba-de-producto.queRecibe: Real opinions from athletes, filmed at the club, to use in its advertising.

jugadores-clinic.queEs: An open skills session led by the club's players or coaches, with a company behind it.
jugadores-clinic.queRecibe: Its brand on an activity that draws young players from other clubs in the area.

jugadores-embajador.queEs: A club player represents the company for the season, beyond a one-off activation.
jugadores-embajador.queRecibe: A well-known face of local sport linked to its business all year round.

jugadores-meet-and-greet.titulo: Fan meet-and-greet at the company's premises
jugadores-meet-and-greet.queEs: Signing shirts, photos and time with the fans, but at the sponsor's bar, shop or premises.
jugadores-meet-and-greet.queRecibe: Bringing people into its own premises, which is what a local business really wants.

eventos-patrocinador.queEs: Team presentation, end-of-season gala, club dinner: any event can have a sponsor.
eventos-patrocinador.queRecibe: Its brand on the poster, at the event and in everything posted about that day.

eventos-naming.titulo: The event takes the company's name
eventos-naming.queEs: The event is called by the sponsor's name everywhere.
eventos-naming.queRecibe: Its name being said every time anyone mentions the event, before, during and after.

eventos-photocall.queEs: The backdrop where everyone takes their photo, with the logos of whoever pays for it.
eventos-photocall.queRecibe: Appearing in every photo people post on their own, which far outnumber the club's.

eventos-catering.queEs: A bar, a restaurant or a caterer provides the food in exchange for visibility.
eventos-catering.queRecibe: Everyone attending tasting what it makes, which is the best advertising for a hospitality business.

eventos-sorteo.queEs: The company provides the prize for the raffle held during the event.
eventos-sorteo.queRecibe: Its product in the hands of someone from the community and its name repeated on stage.

eventos-muestras.queEs: The company hands out product to those attending: drinks, food, merchandise, vouchers.
eventos-muestras.queRecibe: Its product reaching hundreds of people from its own neighbourhood in one afternoon.

eventos-dia-del-club.queEs: The day all the teams play and everyone comes. The biggest event of the year.
eventos-dia-del-club.queRecibe: The busiest day of the whole season, with its brand as host.

eventos-transporte.queEs: A transport company provides the coach to take the team or the fans.
eventos-transporte.queRecibe: Its brand on the trip, with a coach full of club people and guaranteed photos.

torneos-patrocinador.queEs: A club's own tournament is the easiest thing it has to sell: a set date, set people, a visible result.
torneos-patrocinador.queRecibe: Its name on the whole tournament, from poster to trophy, in front of clubs and families from across the area.

torneos-trofeos.queEs: A company pays for the trophies and appears on them.
torneos-trofeos.queRecibe: Its brand on an object that sits on a shelf at home for years.

torneos-mvp.queEs: The company presents the MVP award, with its name on it.
torneos-mvp.queRecibe: The most photographed moment of the tournament, with its representative in the photo.

torneos-camisetas.queEs: Every participant takes home a T-shirt with the sponsor's brand.
torneos-camisetas.queRecibe: Hundreds of T-shirts with its logo spread around the area, still being worn months later.

torneos-avituallamiento.queEs: Drinks and fruit for the participants throughout the day.
torneos-avituallamiento.queRecibe: A cheap way to be present all day and in everyone's hands.

torneos-jornada.titulo: Sponsor of one day or age group
torneos-jornada.queEs: There's no need to sell the whole tournament: one age group or a single day can be sold.
torneos-jornada.queRecibe: Getting into a big tournament with a small contribution.

torneos-zona-empresa.queEs: A space with stalls from several local businesses during the tournament.
torneos-zona-empresa.queRecibe: Selling or getting known all day long, with a captive audience between matches.

torneos-final.queEs: The match with the biggest crowd and most attention of the whole tournament, sold separately.

contenido-resumen-partido.queEs: The video or write-up of what happened in the match, which the club already does every week, with a brand behind it.
contenido-resumen-partido.queRecibe: Being in the most looked-for content every weekend, with no extra effort for anyone.

contenido-fotografia.queEs: Each matchday's photos carry a watermark or a caption with the sponsor.
contenido-fotografia.queRecibe: Appearing in the photos families download, print and share.

contenido-entrevistas.queEs: A series of interviews with players, coaches or club people, with a fixed sponsor.
contenido-entrevistas.queRecibe: A recognisable feature carrying its name all season.

contenido-podcast.queEs: An audio or video show about the club and its league.
contenido-podcast.queRecibe: Spoken mentions, which last longer and are remembered better than a logo.

contenido-reportaje.queEs: A long piece telling who is behind the business and why it backs the club.
contenido-reportaje.queRecibe: A story told properly, which is what makes a neighbour choose its shop over another.

contenido-detras-de-camaras.queEs: Dressing room, travel, warm-up: what isn't seen, which is usually what hooks people most.
contenido-detras-de-camaras.queRecibe: Being in the club's most personal content, the kind people watch to the end.

contenido-cantera.queEs: A feature dedicated to the youth teams, which is what families share most.
contenido-cantera.queRecibe: The content with the widest real reach, because every parent forwards it to the whole family.

contenido-educativo.queEs: The company shares what it knows —a physio explains a stretch, a nutritionist a breakfast— and the club publishes it.
contenido-educativo.queRecibe: Showing it knows its stuff, which sells far better than repeating a logo.

digital-banner-web.queEs: A fixed space on the club's site, seen by anyone checking results or kick-off times.
digital-banner-web.queRecibe: Permanent visibility and a direct link to its own website.

digital-empresa-recomendada.queEs: The club publicly recommends the company to its members and families.
digital-empresa-recomendada.queRecibe: A recommendation with a name attached, which is the most valuable thing a community club can give.

digital-newsletter.queEs: The email the club sends to members and families has a fixed sponsor.
digital-newsletter.queRecibe: Landing in the inbox of people who open that email because they care, not a bought list.

digital-qr.queEs: A poster at the sports hall with a QR code leading to the company's offer for club people.
digital-qr.queRecibe: Being able to measure exactly how many club people reach its business.

digital-pagina-patrocinada.queEs: One specific part of the website —results, youth teams, fixtures— carries a company's name.
digital-pagina-patrocinada.queRecibe: Being linked to what people actually check, which is usually the fixtures and results.

digital-cartel-fichajes.queEs: Posts about new signings, departures and renewals carry the sponsor's logo.
digital-cartel-fichajes.queRecibe: Appearing in the posts most shared outside the club, especially in summer.

retransmision-patrocinador.queEs: If the club streams matches, even on YouTube, that can be sold.
retransmision-patrocinador.queRecibe: Its brand throughout the stream, in front of people who can't make it to the hall but follow the match.

retransmision-logo.queEs: A corner of the picture with the brand, there for the whole match.
retransmision-logo.queRecibe: Well over an hour of continuous presence, not a three-second flash.

retransmision-descanso.queEs: The half-time slot is filled with an advert from the company.
retransmision-descanso.queRecibe: Several minutes all to itself, with the audience already hooked and waiting for the second half.

retransmision-mvp.queEs: When the stream ends the best player is chosen, with the company's name on the award.
retransmision-mvp.queRecibe: A closing moment with its brand and one more post the next day.

retransmision-entrevista.queEs: The after-match interview has a sponsor, just like on TV.
retransmision-entrevista.queRecibe: Appearing at the moment people stay on to hear what happened.

retransmision-clips.queEs: The match clips posted afterwards, carrying the sponsor's brand.
retransmision-clips.queRecibe: Being in the most forwarded content, because it lasts twenty seconds and gets shared on WhatsApp.

familias-descuento.queEs: The company offers club people a special price, and the club spreads the word.
familias-descuento.queRecibe: New customers from its own neighbourhood, without putting in money: it puts in margin.

familias-carnet.queEs: A group of shops gives perks to anyone showing their club card.
familias-carnet.queRecibe: Joining a network of local shops with the club as its backer.

familias-actividad.queEs: A workshop, an afternoon snack, an open day for parents and siblings.
familias-actividad.queRecibe: Quality time with the families, unhurried and not competing with a match.

familias-regalo-navidad.queEs: A small gift for every kid at the club, provided by a company.
familias-regalo-navidad.queRecibe: Its brand on a memorable gift, handed out at the most emotional moment of the year.

familias-sorteo-socios.queEs: A draw open only to club people, which is also a reason to become a member.
familias-sorteo-socios.queRecibe: Being seen as the one giving something, and helping the club sign up members along the way.

familias-campana-comercios.queEs: Several small businesses come in together, each with an affordable contribution.
familias-campana-comercios.queRecibe: A place on the board of the club's friendly shops, within reach of a business that can't sponsor on its own.

tienda-patrocinador-de-la-tienda.queEs: A company pays for the club's first run of merchandise —caps, hoodies, keyrings— and the club sells it and keeps the money.
tienda-patrocinador-de-la-tienda.queRecibe: Its brand next to the crest on everything the club sells that season, and on the stall where it's sold on match days.

tienda-personalizado-con-dorsal.titulo: Personalised items with name and number
tienda-personalizado-con-dorsal.queEs: Keyrings, magnets, mugs or bottle openers with the club crest and, on the back, each player's name and shirt number.
tienda-personalizado-con-dorsal.queRecibe: A local printer or sign maker gets the order, puts its brand on every piece and ends up in every club family's home.

tienda-mercadillo-de-equipaciones.queEs: The club sells off the kits, tracksuits and backpacks from past seasons that are taking up space in the storeroom, at second-hand prices.
tienda-mercadillo-de-equipaciones.queRecibe: Giving its name to the sale day, with its brand on the poster and the stall, in front of every family dropping by to try on sizes.

tienda-venta-a-comision.titulo: A company sells at your matches for a commission
tienda-venta-a-comision.queEs: A shop sets up its stall at home matches and sells its products there. The club takes a percentage of what it sells.
tienda-venta-a-comision.queRecibe: A sales point with a guaranteed audience every matchday, with no rent and no new shop to open.

tienda-prenda-oficial.titulo: The official item of the season
tienda-prenda-oficial.queEs: A cap, a scarf or a fan shirt the club brings out every season for the people in the stands to wear, not the players.
tienda-prenda-oficial.queRecibe: Its logo next to the crest on an item people wear because they want to, all year round in the neighbourhood.

tienda-ropa-de-paseo.queEs: Tracksuit, hoodie and backpack with the crest, for families to buy and kids to wear to school, not just to training.
tienda-ropa-de-paseo.queRecibe: Its brand on clothes worn every day away from the sports hall, which is where they're seen most and where no sponsorship reaches.

tienda-lote-de-bienvenida.queEs: Every child who joins the club gets a pack on their first day: backpack, water bottle, keyring and the crest. A company pays for it.
tienda-lote-de-bienvenida.queRecibe: Being the first thing a new family takes home from the club, with its brand on the pack and in the first-day photo.

tienda-producto-con-el-escudo.titulo: A company product with the club crest
tienda-producto-con-el-escudo.queEs: The bakery makes the club pastry, the winery a label with the crest, the ice-cream shop a flavour named after the team. A share of every unit sold goes to the club.
tienda-producto-con-el-escudo.queRecibe: A product that sells itself locally because it carries the team's crest, and a reason for the club to talk about it across its social media.

local-evento-conjunto.queEs: Club and company organise something together away from the sports hall: in a street, a square, a shopping centre.
local-evento-conjunto.queRecibe: Getting out of its premises and having people link it to the club in front of the whole town.

local-presentacion-producto.queEs: The company launches something new and does it with the team there.
local-presentacion-producto.queRecibe: An event with well-known faces from local sport and coverage from the club.

local-escaparate.titulo: The club in the company's shop window
local-escaparate.queEs: Signed shirt, trophies, poster for the next match: the club decorates the sponsor's premises.
local-escaparate.queRecibe: A shop window the neighbourhood talks about, and a reason to come in and ask.

local-cupones.queEs: Company vouchers given to the people attending a match.
local-cupones.queRecibe: People walking through its door voucher in hand, and an exact count of how many.

local-accion-solidaria.queEs: A food, toy or equipment collection organised by the club and the company together.
local-accion-solidaria.queRecibe: Being seen doing something that matters, which is one of the few things a neighbour really remembers.

local-colegios.queEs: The club visits schools to run a session, with a company behind it.
local-colegios.queRecibe: Reaching the families of the whole school, not just the club's.

necesita-fisioterapia.queEs: Someone to treat the squad's injuries during the season.
necesita-fisioterapia.queRecibe: Ongoing visibility with athletes and families, which is exactly its audience, and patients who come by themselves.

necesita-medico.queEs: Pre-season medicals or cover at home matches.
necesita-medico.queRecibe: Its brand as the club's official medical service and direct access to every family.

necesita-fotografo.queEs: Someone to cover home matches and give the club decent photos every week.
necesita-fotografo.queRecibe: Its credit on every photo the club posts, which is the most constant advertising there is.

necesita-video.queEs: Match highlights, the season launch, pieces for social media.
necesita-video.queRecibe: Its brand on everything that moves at the club, and a showcase for its work in town.

necesita-marketing.titulo: Help with the club's social media
necesita-marketing.queEs: Someone to lend a hand with posts and communications.
necesita-marketing.queRecibe: A real case to show other clients, with measurable results.

necesita-imprenta.queEs: Posters, banners, vinyls, shirt numbers: everything that needs printing through the year.
necesita-imprenta.queRecibe: Its brand on everything the club prints, seen by everyone who passes through the sports hall.

necesita-transporte.queEs: Taking the team to away matches.

necesita-restauracion.queEs: Sandwiches, catering for the gala, food at the tournament.

necesita-alojamiento.queEs: Overnight stays for tournaments or long away trips.
necesita-alojamiento.queRecibe: Its brand linked to the club's trips, and bookings in quiet periods.

necesita-nutricion.queEs: Dietary guidance for the squad or talks for families.
necesita-nutricion.queRecibe: Presenting itself as the expert, in front of an audience already interested.

necesita-asesoria.queEs: Handling the club's accounts, payroll or paperwork.
necesita-asesoria.queRecibe: Being the club's official accountant, with the public recommendation that comes with it.

necesita-informatica.queEs: Maintaining the club's website, email or office computers.
necesita-informatica.queRecibe: Its brand in the website footer and a visible client in town.
